\section[il carabiniere]{il carabiniere — the carabiniere, the military police officer}

\label{lesson:IT-C294-carabiniere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the alarm, then the Italian for the vandal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il carabiniere}
\textbf{il carabiniere} — \textquotedblleft{}the carabiniere, the military police officer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ho chiesto aiuto a un carabiniere.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I asked a carabiniere for help.}
\end{quote}

One of the two main police forces; the other is \emph{la polizia}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{carabiniere} is usually traced to French \emph{carabinier}, a soldier armed with a \emph{carabine}, a short gun. EtymDB derives \emph{carabine} from \emph{carabin} \textquotedblleft{}a dragoon\textquotedblright{}, whose own origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il carabiniere}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il carabiniere}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il carabiniere}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the alarm, then the Italian for the vandal, then say \emph{il carabiniere} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does il carabiniere mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The carabiniere, the military police officer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[il commissariato]{il commissariato — the police station}

\label{lesson:IT-C294-commissariato}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the vandal, then the Italian for the carabiniere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il commissariato}
\textbf{il commissariato} — \textquotedblleft{}the police station\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il commissariato è in fondo alla strada.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police station is at the end of the street.}
\end{quote}

The local office of \emph{la polizia}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{commissariato} is built on \emph{commissario} \textquotedblleft{}commissioner\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Medieval Latin \emph{commissārius}, built on Latin \emph{committere} \textquotedblleft{}to entrust\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{il commissariato}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{il commissariato}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the vandal, then the Italian for the carabiniere, then say \emph{il commissariato} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[la pattuglia]{la pattuglia — the patrol}

\label{lesson:IT-C294-pattuglia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the carabiniere, then the Italian for the police station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la pattuglia}
\textbf{la pattuglia} — \textquotedblleft{}the patrol\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Una pattuglia è arrivata in cinque minuti.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A patrol arrived in five minutes.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Essere di pattuglia} — to be on patrol.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pattuglia} was borrowed from French \emph{patrouille} \textquotedblleft{}patrol\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[la telecamera]{la telecamera — the video camera, the CCTV camera}

\label{lesson:IT-C294-telecamera}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the police station, then the Italian for the patrol.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la telecamera}
\textbf{la telecamera} — \textquotedblleft{}the video camera, the CCTV camera\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le telecamere hanno ripreso tutto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The cameras filmed everything.}
\end{quote}

For photos, \emph{la macchina fotografica}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{telecamera} joins Greek \emph{tēle} \textquotedblleft{}far\textquotedblright{} and \emph{camera}, from Latin \emph{camera} \textquotedblleft{}a vault, a room\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short); EtymDB links it with English \emph{television camera}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[l'inseguimento]{l'inseguimento — the chase, the pursuit}

\label{lesson:IT-C294-inseguimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the patrol, then the Italian for the video camera.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'inseguimento}
\textbf{l'inseguimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the chase, the pursuit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dopo un lungo inseguimento, la polizia l'ha preso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{After a long chase, the police caught him.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{inseguire}, ‘to chase’.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inseguimento} is built on \emph{inseguire} \textquotedblleft{}to chase\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{in-} and \emph{seguire} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{sequī} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the patrol, then the Italian for the video camera, then say \emph{l'inseguimento} again
\end{itemize}
